chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Ibrahim ibn Umar al-Yamani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Allah, Mighty and Majestic, did not send any Prophet at all except that it was in the Knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that when He completed the Religion for him, the prohibition of wine was included in it, and wine did not cease to be unlawful. Indeed, the Religion is merely transformed from one characteristic to another, so if that had been in its entirety (all characteristics at once), they would have been cut off from the Religion.
ai.seo_question: Why was the prohibition of wine not immediate for all Prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the concept of *al-tahwil* (shifting or gradual implementation) in Islamic jurisprudence, asserting that while the essence of wine's prohibition was eternally known to God, its legal burden was eased progressively to accommodate human capacity. Scholars highlight this as a key principle explaining why certain rulings were not revealed all at once, ensuring the Religion remained sustainable for the community rather than becoming an insurmountable burden.
